speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me understand the full picture, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any joint pain or a rash on your palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease (Incomplete). The combination of a rash, fever, and specifically a facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly characteristic. I need to confirm the duration of fever and check for conjunctivitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, and extremity changes like redness or peeling. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C-Reactive_Protein, ESR, Liver_Function_Tests. REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_photo_of_rash, Hands_and_feet_close_up.
